entry.title: MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 & MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 Security Updates Released
entry.content:
MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 and MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 are available now as security software updates for Mac users who are continuing to run those operating systems. Those users will also find Safari 27.2 available as an update.

These updates include hundreds of security patches and fixes making them recommended to all users who are running macOS Tahoe or Sequoia, instead of MacOS 27 Golden Gate.

Separately, Apple has also released MacOS 27.2 Golden Gate, iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, iOS 26.7.2, iPadOS 26.7.2, iOS 18.7.11, iPadOS 18.7.11, watchOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, along with updates to just about every other Apple device, so you’ll want to check for and install updates elsewhere too.

How to Download & Install MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 or MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 Update

Be sure to backup your Mac with Time Machine prior to starting the updates:

  1. From the  Apple menu, go to “System Settings”
  2. Go to “General”, and then go to “Software Update”
  3. Ignore the prominent “MacOS 27.2” banner, and instead look below that for the small “Other Updates” section, where you can find MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 or “MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 available to update instead *

* Note that if you click on the (i) info button to get additional information about the MacOS Tahoe or MacOS Sequoia update, you will find that MacOS 27.2 is selected instead. You need to manually unselect that, and select the update you wish to install, to avoid accidentally installing MacOS Golden Gate.

The Mac will restart to finish installation.

Direct Download MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 & MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 Full Installers

Apple CDN links for the full installers:

You might also appreciate bookmarking our updated list of all avialable MacOS installers as a resource for downloads like these.

MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 Release Notes & MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 Release Notes

Release notes are brief:

This update provides important security fixes and is recommended for all users.

For information on the security content of Apple software updates, please visit this website: https://support.apple.com/100100

Don’t forget to update your other Apple devices and hardware as well, since just about every supported Mac, iPhone, iPad, Apple Watch, HomePod, Apple TV, and Apple Vision Pro, has received an update today, the most prominent being the iOS 27.2 / iPadOS 27.2 updates, and MacOS 27.2 Golden Gate update.

entry.title: Apple Updates MacBook Pro & iMac to M6 Chip, iPad Mini with 8.5″ OLED Display
entry.content:
Apple has released a series of hardware updates this week, including an updated iPad Mini with A20 chip and OLED display, an iMac with M6 chip, and a 14″ MacBook Pro base model with M6 chip. These products were announced ahead of the “Pro and Tell” event set for tomorrow, which is expected to launch a touchscreen MacBook Pro.

14″ MacBook Pro with M6 Chip

The base-model MacBook Pro 14″ now includes an M6 chip with 12-core CPU and GPU, better AI performance, and improved memory bandwidth, Wi-Fi 7 support, and is available in the same color options as before. Notably, the new base model MacBook Pro comes with a 1TB SSD, along with 16GB RAM.

Pricing begins at $1999, with pre-orders on October 28.

iMac with M6 Chip

Apple has updated the 24″ iMac lineup to include the new powerful M6 chip, which boosts performance considerably with a 12-core CPU and 12-core GPU, and improved AI performance. The iMac M6 comes standard with 16GB RAM and a 256GB storage, and is available in the same set of color options as prior models, including green, blue, purple, yellow, orange, red, and silver.

Pricing starts at $1499, with pre-orders starting October 28 and availability on November 6.

iPad Mini with A20 Chip and OLED Display

The iPad Mini has now been updated to include an A20 Pro chip, and the LCD screen has been replaced with a slightly larger 8.5″ OLED display which allows for darker blacks but comes at the cost of PWM which impacts some users eyes (yours truly included). The device also includes a 12MP center stage front-facing camera, wi-fi 7 support, Apple Pencil support, water and dust resistance, and is available in space grey and silverlight colors.

Pricing for iPad Mini now starts at $699 for wi-fi models, and $849 for cellular equipped models. Pre-orders start October 28 for November 6 delivery.

–

Not yet launched, but expected to arrive tomorrow, is the all-new touchscreen MacBook Pro. Stay tuned for more details on that, as the announcement is made.

That all covers the hardware side of things, but don’t forget the software side, where Apple has released a whole bevy of system software updates for nearly every Apple device, including iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, HomePod OS 27.2 with support for Sound Glow, watchOS 27.2, tvOS 27.2, visionOS 27.2, iOS 26.7.2, MacOS 27.2 Golden Gate, and several hundred security patches are included in both MacOS Sequoia 15.8.2 and MacOS Tahoe 26.7.2 (and yes the same security patches are included the other software updates too).

entry.title: Touchscreen MacBook Pro Launched by Apple
entry.content:
Apple has launched two all-new touchscreen MacBook Pro models, with 14″ and 16″ OLED display sizes. This marks a notable reversal from Apple against their longstanding resistance to touch screen laptops due to ergonomic issues.

The new MacBook Pro features a redesigned enclosure, M5 Pro or M5 Max chip options with up to 128GB RAM and 16GB of storage, a smaller Dynamic Island cutout replaces The Notch on the display, and is lighter weight than predecessors, weighing 3lbs for the 14″ model, and 4lbs for the 16″ model. A notable welcome return is the reintroduction of the glowing Apple logo on the back of the MacBook Pro.


There is full gesture support for the touchscreen, allowing for gestures like pinch to zoom, scrolling, and swiping between pages, slides, or Spaces. Apple Pencil is not supported.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro includes a front-facing FaceTime camera, three Thunderbolt 5 / USB-C ports, HDMI port, SDXC card slot, MagSafe for power, and a headphone jack.

The touchscreen display itself is OLED, and available in both 14″ and 16″ sizes, which Apple is calling the PROLED XDR Display. Presumably the display will have perceptible PWM like most OLED and LED-adjacent screens have, which could dissuade some PWM sensitive users from being able to use the Mac.

The 14″ touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $2899, while the 16″ touchscreen MacBook Pro starts at $3399. Pre-orders are live now and the touchscreen MacBook Pro will be available on November 6.

The video embedded below from X shows someone using the touch screen display to interact with MacOS:

And another:

And another:

As noted earlier, the introduction of a touchscreen Mac marks a departure from Apple’s prior stance on the matter. Apple had long been skeptical of touchscreen laptops, with Steve Jobs famously lamenting on the ergonomics of such a device (videos embedded are via X, you can find us there too):

The standard non-touch models of MacBook Pro are still available as well, the base model of which was just spec-bumped to the M6 chip.

The touchscreen MacBook Pro is the fourth major Apple product released this week, adding alongside to the A20 iPad Mini, M6 MacBook Pro, and M6 iMac.

entry.title: How to Boot in Safe Mode on MacBook Air, Neo, & Pro (Apple Silicon)
entry.content:
You may find yourself in a situation when you need to boot into Safe Mode while troubleshooting a MacBook Air, MacBook Neo, or MacBook Pro.

Safe Mode boots a Mac without loading third party login items, system extensions, and non-system fonts. Additionally, Safe Mode runs a disk check to verify the startup disk, clears system caches, and prevents third party drivers from loading, helping to narrow down potential issues, and sometimes even resolve them through the safe mode boot itself.

If you’re unfamiliar with booting into Safe Mode on modern Apple Silicon equipped MacBook laptops, including the Air, Neo, and Pro, it’s a pretty easy process that is the same on all Apple Silicon Macs, including M1, M2, M3, M4, M5, M6, A18 chips.

How to Boot in Safe Mode on MacBook Air, Pro, Neo

  1. If the Mac is currently turned on, you need to turn it off by going go the  Apple menu and selecting “Shut Down”
  2. When the Mac is off, now press and hold the Power button / Touch ID button, and continue holding the Power/Touch ID button until you see “Loading startup options”
  3. At the startup disk screen, now hold down the SHIFT key and click on “Continue in Safe Mode” and select “Macintosh HD” (or your boot disk)

  4. Once Safe Mode has started booting, you can release Shift key

The Mac will now be in Safe Mode, where you can perform whatever troubleshooting tasks you had in mind.

As mentioned before, simply booting into Safe Mode can sometimes remedy an issue if it’s related to a cache or third party extension or tool. If the problem is absent in Safe Mode but you boot normally again and the problem returns, that suggests the issue is related to some third party extension, tool, login item, or otherwise.

And sometimes problems persist in Safe Mode too, which usually suggests a system level problem. I ran into that recently when troubleshooting ‘dasd’ process 100% CPU usage over several days, even in safe mode, and eventually resolved that issue by removing a corrupt system database.

Exiting Safe Mode and Booting Normally Again

  1. Simply restart the Mac as usual to boot the Mac as normal, from the  Apple menu choose “Restart”

This process obviously covers Apple Silicon Mac laptops with Touch ID and the power button, but if you have an older Intel Mac you can use Safe Mode on those Macs too by simply holding Shift key during the entire boot process, arguably a bit easier.

entry.title: First Betas of iOS 27.3 & MacOS 27.3 Available for Testing
entry.content:
Apple has issued the first beta build of iOS 27.3, iPadOS 27.3, and MacOS 27.3 Golden Gate, to users who are participating in the beta testing programs of Apple system software.

iOS 27.3 and MacOS 27.3 betas include a new vertical tab option in Safari, as well as an automatic dark mode feature for Safari. iPhone Duo gains a Reachability feature that pulls the screen content to the side to make interacting with one hand easier, new Standby Mode clock features and options for all iPhones with iOS 27.3, more Siri functionality, and a redesigned Health app. Apple Intelligence is also set to arrive in China with theses releases.

For iPhone, iPad, and Mac users who are participating in the beta system software testing programs, you can download the latest iOS 27.3 beta 1 build in Settings > General > Software Update, whereas Mac users can find MacOS 27.3 beta 1 in System Settings > General > Software Update.

Apple usually goes through multiple iterations of beta software before releasing a final version to the general public, and Apple has previously said that iOS 27.3 will be released this December.

The most recent stable non-beta versions of system software are currently iOS 27.2, iPadOS 27.2, and MacOS 27.2 Golden Gate.

entry.title: How to Enable Sound Glow on HomePod & HomePod Mini
entry.content:
Sound Glow is a snazzy new feature introduced for HomePod (2nd gen and later), and HomePod Mini (1st gen and later) that allows the small display on the top of the smart speaker to show a fun little ambient light effect that reacts to the rhythm, beat, and color of whatever you are playing on the device. It adds a bit of character to the HomePod that is particularly enjoyable in a dimmer or dark room. Curiously, Sound Glow is not enabled by default, so if you wish to use the feature you will have to turn it on manually, which we will show you how to do here.

Sound Glow System Requirements

Sound Glow is compatible with HomePod (2nd gen and later), and HomePod Mini (1st gen and later). The first gen HomePod does not support the feature.

Additionally, Sound Glow requires you to update your HomePod to HomeOS 27.2 (or whatever they’re calling it). That’ll happen automatically if you have a paired iPhone or iPad with iOS 27.2, or a Mac with MacOS 27.2. If your HomePod is not yet updated, you can do that manually from a Mac or iPhone/iPad within the Home app.

You will also want to update Spotify, Podcasts, and other apps, so they can support the feature fully.

How to Enable Sound Glow on HomePod & HomePod Mini

Assuming you meet the requirements and have your devices updated, here’s how to enable Sound Glow, which curiously is not enabled by default:

  1. Open the “Home” app on your iPhone, iPad, or Mac running iOS 27.2 or MacOS 27.2
  2. Long-press or right-click on the HomePod and choose “Accessory Settings”

  3. Scroll down and look for the “Sound Glow” option and toggle it ON

  4. Exit out of Home app
  5. Now open Music.app, Spotify, Podcasts, or another similar compatible app, and play audio through the HomePod to see SoundGlow in action

You should see the colors start to move and change on the little display atop HomePod right away, which will vary depending on the music and beat or what you are listening to.

The Sound Glow setting describes the feature as “Display ambient light that responds to the colors and rhythm of what’s playing.”

Note that some music and audio streams seem to be a little slower to adapt or catch onto Sound Glow, particularly through third party apps, so if you aren’t seeing immediate feedback you might try Music app or Podcasts app, and you’ll want to be sure to update Spotify and other apps to their latest versions just in case too.

If you have a HomePod, try it out yourself, it’s a fun new feature and worth enabling on your Apple smart speakers.

This is obviously for compatible HomePod devices, and it remains to be seen if HomeView will have a similar Sound Glow feature, perhaps on the screen itself, but we will find that out soon.

entry.title: Watch Charlie Brown Thanksgiving Free on Apple TV (2026)
entry.content:
Mark you calendars, because everyone can watch “A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving” for free on Apple TV this November. The 1973 animated Peanuts classic movie will be watchable without a subscription or even a free trial, nearly two weeks before Thanksgiving.

“A Charlie Brown Thanksgiving” will be made available during a free streaming weekend, on Saturday November 14, and Sunday November 15.

The popular classic movie is a 25 minute animated special based on the Peanuts comic strip, and focuses on an unconventional goofy Thanksgiving dinner prepared by Charlie Brown, Snoopy, Woodstock, and the whole Peanuts gang.

Anyone interested in watching Charlie Brown Thanksgiving can use the Apple TV app on any device including iPhone, iPad, Mac, Apple TV, Roku, Amazon Fire TV, and various smart TVs, or even the Apple TV website at tv.apple.com, but only on Nov 14 and Nov 15. If you attempt to access the movie before then, or after then, it will not be available free.

Apple made the announcement of the free watch weekends for Charlie Brown Thanksgiving and Charlie Brown Christmas quietly in September. Charlie Brown Christmas will be available to watch free on December 12 and 13.

And if you do have an Apple TV subscription, whether paid or a free trial, you’ll be able to watch these shows anytime too.

entry.title: Run Mac OS X Tiger, Snow Leopard, Lion, etc on Apple Silicon Macs with Virtual Intel Mac
entry.content:
Apple Silicon Mac users can now install and run any Intel version of MacOS and Mac OS X directly on their modern Mac, with great performance, thanks to the Virtual Intel Mac project.

Virtual Intel Mac, which has a fairly self explanatory name, allows you to run any Intel version of MacOS on a modern Apple Silicon Mac, ranging from Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger to MacOS 11 Big Sur. Yes that means you can install Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6, or OS X Mountain Lion 10.8, right now on your modern Apple Silicon Mac. This allows you to be able to run older 32-bit Intel apps on a modern Mac, and even some PPC apps too, even on Apple Silicon.

Using Virtual Intel Mac is remarkably simple and easy, upon first launch (you’ll probably need to bypass Gatekeeper first) you can choose whichever Intel MacOS version you’d like to run.

Supported Mac OS X versions by Virtual Intel Mac include; Mac OS X Tiger 10.4, Mac OS X Leopard 10.5, Mac OS X Snow Leopard 10.6, Mac OS X Lion 10.7, OS X Mountain Lion 10.8, OS X Mavericks 10.9, OS X Yosemite 10.10, OS X El Capitan 10.11, macOS Sierra 10.12, macOS High Sierra 10.13, macOS Mojave 10.14, macOS Catalina 10.15, macOS Big Sur 11, and MacOS Monterey 12. Later versions of MacOS can be run on a modern Mac as any standard virtual machine by downloading the desired macOS installer or IPSW and setting them up in a virtual machine.

Just pick the version you’d like to install and go through the simple walkthrough, Virtual Intel Mac will then download and install the version of MacOS for you.

You’ll go through the typical installation process of the version of Mac OS X that you chose to install.

Note that some versions of Mac OS X will go through an automatic setup process by the app itself that can take up to 30 minutes

And soon enough, you’ll be at the desktop of your old Mac OS version of choice.

In this screenshot example, Mac OS X 10.4 Tiger is running atop MacOS Golden Gate 27:

Virtual Intel Mac supports USB and audio passthrough, networking, file sharing, remote login, and more, so you can use older hardware and software that is compatible if you’d like to.

This is a really great project, and if you’re a fan of virtualization, emulators, or older versions of MacOS, you’re sure to appreciate Virtual Intel Mac.
